**CA alone:** one justified block, its own material, the fit check, responding to CA's track. **Measure the dome under the text block and the texture budget BEFORE building.** Then the other three.

### ⛔⛔ AMENDED 24 September 2026 — THE TEXT'S MATERIAL IS ETCHED GLASS, EDGE-LIT BY THE RIM. And the first two steps are done

**Carl, 24 September 2026:** *"Etched glass sounds like a great concept. We can rule out metal because of the surroundings issue. The gilded idea is a good thought too and i will take it as a recommendation. It fits the concept."* ⛔ **He tunes it by eye.**

| option | standing |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **ETCHED GLASS, EDGE-LIT** — the body copy is a frosted, etched region IN the glass. When the rim strikes, the etching glows in the tube's colour. | **CHOSEN** |
| **Metal body text** (gilded, reflective) | ⛔ **RULED OUT** — *"because of the surroundings issue"*: a metal letter reflects its environment, which is near-black (RIM-DARK), and the neon lights nothing (D-093). Unlit metal text would read dark. |
| **Gilded ROLE NAMES** with an etched body | ⚠ **RECOMMENDED, NOT RULED OR BUILT** — Carl: *"take it as a recommendation. It fits the concept."* It answers the open "a title that catches the light" question. ⚠ **It carries the same surroundings dependency that ruled metal out for the body**, so it cannot read as intended until the rim is a real light (D-090) or the environment is fixed (RIM-DARK). |

**Why etched glass — the physics is the argument (§14a).** Engrave a glass or acrylic sheet, light its edge, and the light travels inside the sheet until the engraving lets it escape: the letters light up and the clear glass stays dark. **These cards have that construction: a glass face with a light-source tube around its rim.** The glowing text is therefore caused by the world, not laid on top of it. It is also a real signage technique, which fits the showcase brief.

**How it behaves:**
- **One layer moves** (D-091, the opal rule). The glow reads the card's existing D-093 brightness track at a small depth, so every stutter reaches the words on the same frame.
- **Unlit, the etch reads as pale frost on clear glass.** That turns the open question *"readable before the neon, or revealed by it?"* into ONE dial: how strongly the etch reads unlit. The material serves either answer.
- **It depends on nothing unbuilt**: no ceiling, no real rim light, no env-map fix. That is exactly what separates it from the metal option.

**Carl's by eye, not asserted here:** the etch's unlit visibility; the glow's depth on the track; whether the glow falls off from the rim toward the centre (real edge-lit glass does). ⚠ **Measure the glow's hue on screen:** ACES turned the navy tube cyan (D-093).

## D-096 — The Lint Baseline's HISTORY Leaves CLAUDE.md. The Rule Stays

**Date:** 2026-10-12
**Status:** APPROVED
**Authority:** Human Founder — Carl. *"npm install * CLAUDE.md decisions.md you have permission to use these files and to act on your recommendations."* Scope confirmed the same day.

**Decision:** `CLAUDE.md`'s `Error handling` keeps the RULE — the baseline is `1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)`, any warning is a regression, the four suppressions are a debt named at their lines — and points here. The HISTORY below moved out of it verbatim, because `CLAUDE.md` loads into every session and the history is needed only when the baseline is in question.

- ⛔ **THE INK — NEAR-BLACK #0a0a0a ON A FACE KEPT BRIGHT (the Builder's choice under Carl's 4.5:1 ruling, his to overrule).** The reason is pass 3: a light can only ADD to a metal's brightness, so dark ink on a lit face GAINS contrast as the moving light passes, while white ink on a dark face would lose it each time the highlight crossed the words — at the arc's face-on moment, behind them. So the studio's brief: everything behind the label bright; the chrome's contrast at the ENDS (narrow strips against dark sides) and the rim.
- **The measure** (`live-work/scripts/whoweare-pass2-capture.mjs`): the label hidden, the bare metal read at EVERY pixel of its text box (81.5 × 21, 1,701 px), WCAG contrast against each; the verdict is the WORST pixel. Take 3: a steeper gradient, worst 4.19:1 — a miss. **Take 4: upper 1.45 / front 0.95 / lower 0.7 → worst pixel 5.02:1, median 6.85:1** — the dome has form and the label clears 4.5 everywhere. ⚠ NOT YET MEASURED UNDER THE MOVING LIGHT — owed in pass 3, along its whole path (Carl's *"On the light motion"*).

We need a complementary colour, possibly light blue."*).** ⚰️ Near-black (take 4) set aside. ⚠ **The principle put to Carl first:** contrast is BRIGHTNESS, not hue — a light ink needs a DARK face, the reverse of take 4; and the risk moves to pass 3, because the moving light can only brighten the metal, so its highlight crossing the words (at the arc's face-on moment, on the flat top) now LOWERS the contrast — its strength and spread must keep the worst pixel ≥ 4.5. **Take 5:** ice blue **#cfe6ff** on a deep teal face (tent 0.26/0.4/0.2) — worst pixel 4.53:1, no margin (not shown). **Take 6: the face dimmed a step (0.21 / 0.33 / 0.17), the blue kept → worst pixel 5.20:1, median 6.93:1** (the paler #e4f2ff would have bought margin by moving the colour toward white; the face moved instead). Put to Carl.

**Status: APPROVED (direction) — Carl, 15 October 2026, session 2. The plan is NOT yet written; it goes through the plan-review gate (`handoff-protocol.md` §2.5) and is proven on one page before rollout.**

**What was found.** Carl's `devicePixelRatio` read 1.36 for the whole build — Windows Text size 136% (D-051's 15 October tail, corrected). His layout viewport was ~**1412 × 795** CSS px, not 1920 × 1080. **Every approval on the site was judged at 1.36×.** At 1.0 the same pages draw at ~74% of the size they were composed at. **Date:** 2026-10-19. **Status: BRIEF — recorded as given; nothing designed or built.**
**Authority:** Human Founder — Carl: *"the boxes are all enclosed. We need to distinguish betwwen them. But instead of enclosing them completely, we could do something just in the 4 corners of each box. A simple 90deg line is not what im after. The word that comes to mind is Ornate. Teal is used in Sect 4. We should use Gold in Sect 2 and platinum Blue is Sect 3. Thats 28 corner pieces. They can all be the same, differing only in colour. 3D with Three js and very subtle light that suggests that they are 3D. Light that can have very little motion. Stll restrained but looking very classy, high end. We can create a design in a proto bench. Go look at brand assets. See the gold logo, blue logo and the LOTR logo.
